sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, which learn from vast amounts of text data. This training helps them predict what words come next in a sentence.

sections.title: How LLMs Process Text
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are transformed into numerical representations known as embeddings, which capture the meanings and relationships between words. This process allows LLMs to understand context and generate relevant responses.

sections.title: The Role of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or instructions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. The way we phrase these prompts can greatly influence the quality of the answers we receive. By carefully designing prompts, we can improve the relevance and accuracy of the LLM's output.

sections.title: Enhancing LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like Automatic Prompt Engineering and Chain-of-Thought prompting help refine how LLMs respond to complex tasks. These methods encourage the model to think step-by-step, which is especially useful for multi-step reasoning tasks. This structured approach aims to reduce errors and improve the reliability of the answers.

sections.title: Challenges and Solutions
sections.body: Despite their capabilities, LLMs can produce incorrect or misleading information, known as hallucinations. To address this, researchers are developing tools that automatically improve prompts and ensure clearer instructions. This helps make LLMs more effective and trustworthy, especially in educational settings.
